item.title: Indiana housing overhaul bill advances by one vote as senators warn of 'one-size-fits-all' risks
item.description: Supporters say state action is needed to boost housing supply, but critics question whether the bill will actually lower costs.

item.title: Bloomington tornado leaves path of destruction on city's west side
item.description: A storm that barreled across Indiana Thursday night brought strong winds and hail to the west side of Bloomington.

item.title: Officials break ground on national security industrial hub at Crane
item.description: State officials broke ground Thursday on a new national security industrial hub near Naval Weapons Station Crane.

item.title: New law limits state-level public hearings on nuclear power facilities
item.description: The law comes as state lawmakers increasingly look toward nuclear energy to address rising electricity costs.

item.title: Indiana House supports an extension of the syringe service programs with new requirements
item.description: The Indiana House of Representatives passed a bill extending state approval for syringe services programs, adding new requirements.

item.title: Indianapolis to receive over $13 million to invest across the city
item.description: Indianapolis will receive over thirteen million dollars as part of a federal program known as Community Project Funding. The funds are awarded to local governments to invest in housing, public health, infrastructure, crime prevention and workforce development.

item.title: Indiana's Nick Goepper knocked out of bronze medal on final run of Olympic freestyle halfpipe
item.description: Nick Goepper from Lawrenceburg, Indiana, the only Hoosier in the Winter Olympics, was knocked out of bronze medal position on the final run of the freestyle skiing halfpipe competition Friday.

item.title: IU President Whitten gets $100,000 raise, annual salary now $1 million
item.description: Indiana University’s Board of Trustees approved a $100,000 raise for President Pamela Whitten today, putting her salary at $1 million.

item.title: How Indianapolis' new public editor is working to rebuild trust in local media
item.description: The Poynter Institute announced the appointment of Tracey Compton as the Indianapolis Public Editor. She will cover all newsroom that serve the city, working to rebuild trust in local media.

item.title: ICE protestors march to Gov. Braun's mansion
item.description: Hundreds of ICE protestors joined a cold, Sunday evening march on Indianapolis’ north side.
